lines.text: What is a tan, really? Pigment, parked over each cell's nucleus.
lines.phonemes: wˌɒt ɪz ɐ tˈan, ɹˈiəlɪ? pˈɪɡmənt, pˈɑːkt ˌəʊvəɹ ˈiːtʃ sˈɛlz njˈuːklɪəs.

lines.text: Brown pigment called melanin sits inside your skin's cells. After ultraviolet light, it can move to sit over each cell's nucleus, like a small cap.
lines.phonemes: bɹˈaʊn pˈɪɡmənt kˈɔːld mˈɛlənɪn sˈɪts ɪnsˈaɪd jɔː skˈɪnz sˈɛlz. ˈaftəɹ ˌʊltɹɐvˈaɪəlɪt lˈaɪt, ɪt kan mˈuːv tə sˈɪt ˌəʊvəɹ ˈiːtʃ sˈɛlz njˈuːklɪəs, lˈaɪk ɐ smˈɔːl kˈap.

lines.text: That cap works like a natural sunscreen, absorbing and scattering ultraviolet light. In skin samples exposed to UVB, cells with a cap had less DNA damage.
lines.phonemes: ðat kˈap wˈɜːks lˈaɪk ɐ nˈatʃəɹəl sˈʌnskɹiːn, ɐbsˈɔːbɪŋ and skˈatəɹɪŋ ˌʊltɹɐvˈaɪəlɪt lˈaɪt. ɪn skˈɪn sˈampəlz ɛkspˈəʊzd tuː jˌuːvˌiːbˈiː , sˈɛlz wɪð ɐ kˈap had lˈɛs dˌiːˌɛnˈeɪ dˈamɪdʒ.

lines.text: The more melanin a cell held, the more protection it had. So the shield is real, but its strength varies from cell to cell. In lab-grown skin cells, the long rays, UVA, set off cap-building through a light sensor.
lines.phonemes: ðə mˈɔː mˈɛlənɪn ɐ sˈɛl hˈɛld, ðə mˈɔː pɹətˈɛkʃən ɪt hˌad. sˌəʊ ðə ʃˈiːld ɪz ɹˈiəl, bˌʌt ɪts stɹˈɛŋθ vˈeəɹiz fɹɒm sˈɛl tə sˈɛl. ɪn lˈabɡɹˈəʊn skˈɪn sˈɛlz, ðə lˈɒŋ ɹˈeɪz, jˌuːvˌiːˈeɪ , sˈɛt ˈɒf kˈapbˈɪldɪŋ θɹuː ɐ lˈaɪt sˈɛnsə.

lines.text: Here is the twist. Caps lower the damage, but do not erase it. The effect depends on how much melanin a cell holds.
lines.phonemes: hˈiəɹ ɪz ðə twˈɪst. kˈaps lˈəʊə ðə dˈamɪdʒ, bˌʌt duːnˌɒt ɪɹˈeɪz ɪt. ðɪ ɪfˈɛkt dɪpˈɛndz ˌɒn hˌaʊ mˈʌtʃ mˈɛlənɪn ɐ sˈɛl hˈəʊldz.

lines.text: So a tan is pigment gathered over each cell's nucleus. It lowers damage, but does not erase it.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ ɐ tˈan ɪz pˈɪɡmənt ɡˈaðəd ˌəʊvəɹ ˈiːtʃ sˈɛlz njˈuːklɪəs. ɪt lˈəʊəz dˈamɪdʒ, bˌʌt dʌznˌɒt ɪɹˈeɪz ɪt.

lines.text: Next: the brick wall on your skin. Which part holds water in?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: ðə bɹˈɪk wˈɔːl ˌɒn jɔː skˈɪn. wˌɪtʃ pˈɑːt hˈəʊldz wˈɔːtəɹ ˈɪn?
